'''''Coronilla valentina''''', the '''shrubby scorpion-vetch''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref>'''smokebush''', '''scorpion vetch''' or '''bastard senna''',<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/4421/Coronilla-valentina/Details | title = ''Coronilla valentina'' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Coronilla]]'' of the legume [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Fabaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to the [[Mediterranean Basin]], and introduced into Kenya and the United States.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" /> It is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|80|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide, with pea-like foliage and fragrant, brilliant yellow flowers in spring and summer, followed by slender pods.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref> [[Carl Linnaeus|Linnaeus]] observed that the flowers, remarkably fragrant in the daytime, are almost scentless at night.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Curtis|first=William|year=1787|title=Coronilla glauca|journal=[[The Botanical Magazine]]|volume=1|pages=Pl. 13|url=http://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Botanical_Magazine/Volume_1/13}}</ref>

In cultivation it is fairly hardy, but prefers Mediterranean conditions, with shelter and warm sunshine. The [[subspecies]] ''C. valentina'' subsp. ''glauca''<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''C. valentina'' subsp. ''glauca''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/98759/Coronilla-valentina-subsp-glauca/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> ([[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''C. glauca'') and its cultivar 'Citrina'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''C. valentina'' subsp. ''glauca'' 'Citrina'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/53148/Coronilla-valentina-subsp-glauca-Citrina/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 22 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2018}}</ref>
